newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco unit says FTC used wrong data.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco unit says FTC used wrong data.

text.p: R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco, said Tuesday that three percent of underage cigarette buyers purchase the Camel brand, not the 13 percent recently cited by Federal Trade Commission staff.

"After reviewing a transcript of last Wednesday's FTC news conference, we understand why news reports focused on the numbers cited by commission staff," said Guy Blynn, vice president and deputy general counsel for R.J. Reynolds.
Blynn accused the FTC of "disingenuously" representing to the press a much higher percentage of underage Camel buyers.
He said the commission knows that the 1993 data of 13 percent have been superseded by more recent figures.
The company cited a survey conducted in April and May 1997 by Audits & Surveys Worldwide.
